Products

Three products, one idea:
your work belongs to you.

Recall keeps your knowledge, Launch sells what you build, and Atlas makes both tangible. Each product stands on its own — together they're a system.

Bastra.Recall

Live

The open-source memory for your AI assistants.

Save in Claude Code, recall in Claude Desktop — your knowledge moves with you between tools instead of dying with each chat. MIT-licensed, runs locally on your machine, and is under active development.

  • MCP server, CLI, REST & Skill — one vault for all agents
  • Documents, decisions, lessons — searchable with OCR
  • No account, no cloud requirement, no lock-in

Bastra.Atlas

In development

The native memory cockpit for macOS.

Your Bastra vault as an app: search, manage, connect — everywhere in your system. This is where it all began, and where we return once Launch is done.

  • Native Swift app, no Electron
  • Vault, clipboard & documents in one place
  • Built on Bastra.Recall

What we stand for

Four principles, no fine print.

These four sentences decide what we build — and what we don't. They apply to every product, from the OSS repo to Bastra.Atlas.

01

Local & private

Your data stays on your machine. No forced account, no cloud requirement, no lock-in — privacy is architecture, not a feature flag.

02

Open source first

The foundation — Bastra.Recall — is MIT-licensed and developed in the open. What we promise, you can read in the code.

03

Companion, not replacement

Bastra doesn't compete with Claude, Cursor, or ChatGPT — it makes them better. We build the layer alongside: memory, sales, overview.

04

We use what we build

Bastra Technologies runs on Bastra products. Every feature is first the answer to a problem of our own — then a selling point.

About Bastra Technologies

One product led to the next.

Not a patchwork portfolio, but a chain: each product grew out of building the previous one — and proves itself by us using it every day.

  1. 01

    Bastra.Atlas needed a memory

    We built a native memory cockpit for macOS — and realized: the memory behind it is the real product. It became standalone, open, and cross-tool.

  2. 02

    The memory became Bastra.Recall

    Recall went live as an open-source project: a memory layer that connects AI assistants via MCP. At launch the next problem showed up — sales, blog, and reach cost more time than building.

  3. 03

    The launch became Bastra.Launch

    So we built the launch system right alongside: self-hosted, multi-brand, with Stripe checkout and a social media cockpit. [hostname-redacted] itself runs on it — each product is the proof for the next.
